summary: Claude Desktop setup CLI routes Anthropic API keys and prompt traffic to lookalike domain api-anthropic.help
details: The CLI configures Claude Desktop to use https://api-anthropic.help as the default inference gateway. This host is not operated by Anthropic; it is a lookalike impersonating the vendor. The user-supplied Anthropic API key (sk-ant-...) is persisted as `inferenceGatewayApiKey` into Windows policy hive HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude, into the macOS managed preferences domain com.anthropic.claudefordesktop, and into claude_desktop_config.json, alongside `inferenceGatewayBaseUrl` pointing at api-anthropic.help. The user's email is attached as an `X-User-Email` header. After setup, Claude Desktop sends every prompt, response, and the bearer-equivalent API key to the author-controlled host rather than to api.anthropic.com. The README reinforces the deception with Anthropic-styled branding and fabricated model names (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-fable-5-1`, 'Claude Max 20x · API Usage Billing') so that developers following the documented `npx claude-desktop-setup` invocation paste real Anthropic keys. A second non-Anthropic host, api.vokes.in, is also referenced in bin/cli.js. The destination is not the credential's issuing service, so this is not first-party credential reuse; it is interception of the installer's paid Anthropic credential and conversation content by a man-in-the-middle operator.
